title: U.S. Wants to Compete for a World Expo Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on May 3, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

U.S. Wants to Compete for a World Expo Act

(Sec. 3) This bill calls for: (1) the United States to rejoin the Bureau of International Expositions (BIE) to promote global branding, domestic job creation, and U.S. tourism; and (2) the Department of State to facilitate the timely submission of a request to rejoin the BIE.

(Sec. 4) The bill authorizes the State Department to: (1) take necessary actions for the United States to rejoin the BIE, and (2) accept contributions for such purpose.

(Sec. 5) Nothing in this bill may be construed to authorize any obligation or expenditure prohibited by provisions of the Admiral James W. Nance and Meg Donovan Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 2000 and 2001 relating to limitations on the obligation or expenditure of funds by the State Department for a U.S. pavilion or exhibit at an international exposition or world's fair registered by the BIE. Such Act is amended to prohibit State Department employees in their official capacity from soliciting funds to pay expenses for such a U.S. pavilion or exhibit.

summary.headline: This 2017 law asks the State Department to help the United States rejoin the Bureau of International Expositions, the group that approves world's fairs.
summary.what_it_does: The law states that the United States should rejoin the Bureau of International Expositions, a group that oversees world's fairs and similar large international exhibitions. It directs the State Department to help submit a request to rejoin in a timely way. It also lets the State Department take needed steps to rejoin and accept outside money for that purpose. Finally, it says the law does not allow spending that older foreign relations rules prohibit for U.S. pavilions at expos, and it bars State Department employees acting in their official role from asking for money to pay for such pavilions.

who_it_affects.how: It is directed to help the United States rejoin the Bureau of International Expositions and is allowed to accept outside contributions for that effort.
They are barred from asking for donations in their official role to pay for a U.S. pavilion or exhibit at an international exposition.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations that might give money for U.S. expo participation
who_it_affects.how: They may be asked to contribute, since the State Department is allowed to accept contributions for the rejoining effort.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on May 8, 2017.
